data.context: Executive Summary From late 2013 onwards, several banks and financial institutions have been attacked by an unknown group of cybercriminals.

evidence.quote: have been attacked by an unknown group of cybercriminals

data.context: An analysis of the campaign has revealed that the initial infections were achieved using spear phishing emails that appeared to be legitimate banking communications, with Microsoft Word 97 - 2003 (.doc) and Control Panel Applet (.CPL) files attached.

evidence.quote: the initial infections were achieved using spear phishing emails

data.context: The email attachments exploit vulnerabilities in Microsoft Office 2003, 2007 and 2010 (CVE-2012-0158 and CVE-2013-3906) and Microsoft Word (CVE-20141761).

evidence.quote: exploit vulnerabilities in Microsoft Office 2003, 2007 and 2010 (CVE-2012-0158 and CVE-2013-3906)

data.context: Once the vulnerability is successfully exploited, the shellcode decrypts and executes the backdoor known as Carbanak .

evidence.quote: the vulnerability is successfully exploited, the shellcode decrypts and executes

data.context: Carbanak is a remote backdoor (initially based on Carberp), designed for espionage, data exfiltration and to provide remote access to infected machines.

evidence.quote: initially based on Carberp

data.context: Based on the results of this operation, the attackers use different lateral movement tools in order to get access to the critical systems in the victim´s infrastructure.

evidence.quote: the attackers use different lateral movement tools

data.context: They then install additional software such as the Ammyy Remote Administration Tool, or even compromise SSH servers.

evidence.quote: compromise SSH servers

data.context: Notably, some of the latest versions of the analyzed Carbanak malware appear not to use any Carberp source code.

evidence.quote: use any Carberp source code
